articles.title_orig: Windy weddings and rocky cruises: How East Coasters are braving the nor'easter this weekend
articles.title_zh: Windy weddings and rocky cruises: How East Coasters are braving the nor'easter this weekend
articles.content_orig:
John Garrisi, left, and Gaige Graf move an outdoor table away from the shorefront during the early stages of a nor'easter storm on Friday. Robert F. Bukaty/AP hide caption
Talia Manno opened her door on Saturday morning to waves lapping halfway up the front steps to her Atlantic City, N.J., home.
"It got up to my fifth step," Manno said. "I was really freaking out."
Manno, a lifelong resident, said the last time water came that high was during Hurricane Sandy .
"Even if you live here and you see high tide and flooding, that was really scary and it happened so fast," she said.
Manno is among tens of millions of people from the mid-Atlantic through the coast of Maine who are in the path of a powerful and rare September nor'easter that is bringing coastal flooding, heavy rain and high winds this weekend.
Nearly 80,000 people were without power across New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and Massachusetts, as of Saturday evening, according to the PowerOutage.com map. The storm is expected to continue hitting the Jersey Shore, New York City, and Eastern Massachusetts into Sunday, according to NWS.
Videos posted on social media Saturday showed streets inundated with water in New Jersey, and massive waves hitting the coast . In New York City, people were seen kayaking in the streets . New Jersey and New York declared states of emergency in counties across the two states, including in New York City.
Francis Tarasiewicz, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service in Massachusetts, said wind gusts along the coast could reach up to 60 miles per hour this weekend. This nor'easter comes earlier than the typical October through May storm season, he said, and will last longer than normal.
Spectators watch wave break during a nor'easter storm on Saturday in Hampton, N.H. Robert F. Bukat/AP hide caption
"Many nor'easters affect the area over the course of about a day," he said. "It's a quick punch of strong winds, in many cases, heavy snow or rain." But, Tarasiewicz said, "with this one, we're looking at about a 48-hour period of winds greater than 35 to 40 miles per hour across the area."
The nor'easter is also making travel difficult. More than 1,000 flights were canceled Saturday with thousands more delayed, according to data from FlightAware . Ferry services on Cape Cod and in Rhode Island were disrupted, and Amtrak canceled several trains due to the weather and downed wires.
Off the coast of New York, the strong winds made for a rough cruise ride for Jessica Lisboa. She brought green apples, ginger ale and an acupressure anti-nausea bracelet to prepare for the Bermuda-bound cruise.
"Let me not sugarcoat it. Was it wild? Yeah, sure. It was a little wild," Lisboa said. "It felt honestly like a roller coaster." Still, she considered it a worthwhile adventure.
The nor'easter also took out a number of events planned for the weekend. Oceans Calling, one of Maryland's biggest music festivals, was canceled on Friday. An AC/DC concert in New Jersey was rescheduled. The Boston Red Sox announced they would move their game against the Chicago Cubs.
Some East Coasters found a way to adapt.
When Olga Ostrovetsky picked a date in September for her small outdoor wedding, she envisioned a beautiful, fall day.
But as she got ready to tie the knot in Wallkill, N.Y., she said, "It's very, very windy."
At first bummed, she's now finding the positives in the disruption.
"It's kind of fitting, to be honest, because my fiancé and I met and it was a torrential downpour," she said. "We met on a day like this, and we're also getting married on a day like this," she said.
As for Manno, the Atlantic City resident, is planning to spend Saturday night with family away from the coast. After this nor'easter, she said she doesn't know how much longer she'll live in the area.
"As the years pass, it seems like it's just getting more and more flooding," she said. "It's crazy."

articles.title_zh: Trump says he approved new fuel economy standards ending Biden-era electric vehicle mandate
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump on Saturday said he approved new fuel economy standards , reversing former President Joe Biden's stricter policies meant to fuel electric vehicle adoption.
Since the Corporate Average Fuel Economy, or CAFE, standards were established in 1975, they have been periodically updated, typically to make vehicles more efficient. Under former President Joe Biden's standards , automakers would have had to increase the fuel efficiency of their passenger cars and light trucks to roughly 50 miles per gallon by 2031. The stricter standards were designed to incentivize electric vehicle production and sales in the U.S.
Trump presented the policy change as a boon for both automakers and consumers, though the final standards have not yet been publicly detailed.
"These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America. That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore," he wrote in the Truth Social post . "Every Manufacturer, from General Motors to Ford to Stellantis, has called me wanting to build here, and now they can!"
The regulatory change would fulfill a campaign promise from Trump to rescind policies that encouraged or incentivized electric vehicles.
It is unclear what the final fuel economy standards will be, although Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy previously said that they would be sharply lower than the Biden-era policies.
Weaker fuel economy standards mean that automakers can produce more pickup trucks and SUVs, which are much more profitable than smaller cars but have worse gas mileage. Electric vehicles also become much less attractive to automakers, although some companies, like General Motors , have said that they will still make them.

articles.title_zh: As Hurricane Nolo stalls near Hawaii’s Big Island, serious flooding likely
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Nolo weakened slightly to a Category 1 storm Saturday as it began to move away from Hawaii, the National Hurricane Center said , but it was still expected to lash Hawaii's Big Island and Maui with heavy rains through the weekend.
The storm was inching west late Saturday morning local time at just 5 mph, the NHC said. It was forecast to remain well south of Hawaii's two big islands, although it was expected to strengthen into a major hurricane on Sunday and Monday before weakening next week.
President Trump on Friday approved an emergency declaration for Hawaii that will provide federal resources and assistance to the state in its recovery from Nolo, Hawaii Gov. Josh Green said.
Nolo had maximum sustained winds of 90 mph, making it a Category 1 hurricane. This comes after it had strengthened Friday into a Category 2 storm with 105-mph winds. The hurricane center, however, said it would likely re-strengthen Sunday and become a major hurricane, which is defined as a Category 3 storm or stronger.
Hurricane-force winds were extending outward up to 35 miles from Nolo's core and tropical storm-force winds extended outward up to 150 miles.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for Hawaii County — the Big Island — which could see over two feet of rain. Catastrophic and life-threatening flash flooding is possible on the Big Island through the weekend, forecasters warned. A hurricane watch for the island was canceled.
A tropical storm watch was in effect for Maui County.
Nolo could bring up to 25 inches of rain to the eastern and southern portions of the Big Island, forecasters said, and the island's western areas could see 1 to 2 inches of rain. For Maui, 4 to 8 inches is possible. The rest of Hawaii is likely to get 1 to 3 inches, with 5 at most, enough to trigger isolated flooding, forecasters said.
All state parks on the Big Island and on Maui will be closed because of the storm, the state's Department of Land and Natural Resources said.
Nolo formed as another storm, Hurricane Polo , continued to swirl in the Pacific, off Mexico's southwestern coast.
The latest storms add to an unusually active season in the Pacific. Earlier this month, Hurricane Lowell brought damaging winds and heavy rain to the western Hawaiian islands of Kauai and Niihau, bringing down trees, damaging roads and knocking out power for thousands.

President Donald Trump on Saturday said he approved new fuel economy standards , reversing former President Joe Biden's stricter policies meant to fuel electric vehicle adoption.
Since the Corporate Average Fuel Economy, or CAFE, standards were established in 1975, they have been periodically updated, typically to make vehicles more efficient. Under former President Joe Biden's standards , automakers would have had to increase the fuel efficiency of their passenger cars and light trucks to roughly 50 miles per gallon by 2031. The stricter standards were designed to incentivize electric vehicle production and sales in the U.S.
Trump presented the policy change as a boon for both automakers and consumers, though the final standards have not yet been publicly detailed.
"These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America. That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore," he wrote in the Truth Social post . "Every Manufacturer, from General Motors to Ford to Stellantis, has called me wanting to build here, and now they can!"
The regulatory change would fulfill a campaign promise from Trump to rescind policies that encouraged or incentivized electric vehicles.
It is unclear what the final fuel economy standards will be, although Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy previously said that they would be sharply lower than the Biden-era policies.
Weaker fuel economy standards mean that automakers can produce more pickup trucks and SUVs, which are much more profitable than smaller cars but have worse gas mileage. Electric vehicles also become much less attractive to automakers, although some companies, like General Motors , have said that they will still make them.

President Trump waves to the media on the South Lawn of the White House on September 26, 2026 in Washington, D.C. Trump is traveling to Knoxville, Tennessee to attend the University of Tennessee vs. University of Texas College football game. Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images North America hide caption
President Trump said on Saturday that he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump said the deal "would not be acceptable," speaking to reporters as he was departing the White House, without giving further explanation.
"I like making a deal too," he said. "But, I'm not — that deal would not be acceptable."
"They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Trump added.
Iran made the proposal, which also called for resuming negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, at the United Nations General Assembly meetings in New York this week.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters on Friday that Iran conveyed to the U.S. through Qatar a "concrete seven-day plan" to reopen the strait.
Iran initially closed the strait after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. The repeated closures have caused major disruptions to the world's oil supply.
"If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi said on Friday. "The choice now rests with the United States."
The Iranian proposal is similar to a "memorandum of understanding" agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June . It would have temporarily ended fighting and restarted ceasefire talks.
The MoU gave Iran relief from a U.S. naval blockade. The U.S. eased sanctions and freed up frozen Iranian assets. In return, Iran promised not to seek a nuclear weapon and said it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
The June agreement collapsed after disputes over the memo's vague wording, including language related to who would control the strait. The U.S. and Iran resumed strikes soon after.
"The actions that the United States should take are not new," Araghchi said. "They are all already in the MoU. They are already under the commitments of the United States. So we don't see any difficulty to implement them."
In a prerecorded interview with CBS set to air Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran will abide by its commitments and said the U.S. needs to show "that it does not intend to overthrow our government or our administration."
"If the United States agrees to proceed in that way, everything will return to the way it was before," Pezeshkian said to CBS. "Because right now, it's the United States that has blocked our way, and naturally, Iran has also blocked the way from its side. These are things that both sides need to open up first; then we can sit down at the negotiating table and discuss other issues at hand."
Pezeshkian said if the U.S. accepts the Iranian proposal on reopening the strait and resuming nuclear negotiations, Iran would allow U.N. nuclear inspectors to enter the country.
NPR's Hadeel Al-Shalchi and Emily Feng contributed reporting.

Trump, Iran’s Pezeshkian set for ‘dramatic’ UNGA as Washington restricts Tehran’s delegation, former White House official warns.
President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are set to converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) this week, setting up what former White House officials describe as a "dramatic" diplomatic moment, with Tehran’s delegation effectively "captive" under U.S. restrictions amid heightened Middle East tensions.
Pezeshkian, for one, is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday, Reuters and Iran's semi-official news agency, Mehr, reported Sunday, with Trump at the rostrum on Tuesday.
"The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment," Theo Wold , former acting assistant attorney general and White House domestic policy advisor, told Fox News Digital.
PUTIN, XI AND IRAN'S PEZESHKIAN DESCEND ON INDIA FOR HIGH-STAKES BRICS SUMMIT AMID ESCALATING GLOBAL TENSIONS
President Donald Trump addresses the 80th United Nations General Assembly in New York, Sept. 23, 2025. (Reuters/Shannon Stapleton)
"For the Iranians, the limitation is going to be that there's going to be less access to the international press and less ability for them to essentially poke the Trump administration in the eye," Wold added before noting that it is "pretty sensible to allow them to participate in the international forum and to discuss whatever issues they think are pertinent to their regime and then tell them to go home."
The high-profile gathering also comes as Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran amid the almost seven-month war. Tehran, meanwhile, has set seven conditions for talks with Washington, according to Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei .
Iran also warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, Reuters reported.
While the U.S. approved visas for Iran’s delegation earlier this week, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the State Department has placed strict limits on Iranian movements while in Manhattan.
As the host country under a 1947 U.N. agreement, the United States generally must facilitate the entry and transit of foreign representatives traveling to U.N. headquarters , including officials from adversarial nations.
"While ordinary Iranians endure brutal repression, water and electricity shortages, and soaring inflation, the regime's officials want to go on shopping sprees in New York. Not on our watch," U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X.
UN WATCHDOG SLAMS POTENTIAL ELECTION OF IRAN TO PANEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS SWAY: 'LUNATICS RUNNING THE ASYLUM'
Pezeshkian accused the U.S. of a "grave betrayal" at the United Nations General Assembly on Sept. 24, 2025, in New York City. (Jeenah Moon/Reuters)
For Washington, Wold said the U.S. is not obligated to give them unrestricted access beyond diplomatic responsibilities.
"Here, the delegation will be restricted to their accommodation in New York City and the U.N. headquarters there in Manhattan," Wold clarified.
He characterized the move by Washington as a way of telling the delegation it could participate in official discussions but not "go and buy a bunch of microwaves or a small car at Costco or a dealership in the greater New York area."
"Some of the restrictions fully recognize that when Iran comes to New York for UNGA, really it's about them lining their pockets and going on shopping sprees to get household appliances and Rolex watches," Wold said. "They're not going to be going on shopping sprees. They're certainly not going to be hitting up Michelin-starred restaurants in greater Manhattan.
"They also go to Sam’s Club and Walmart and Costco. And that was one of the specific prohibitions issued by the State Department this week: to contact those big-box retailers that require a basic membership and say, ‘You’re not to transact or do any business with Iranians when they arrive, and you’re to notify us when they do.’"
KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian walks to meet with France's President Emmanuel Macron during the General Assembly at U.N. headquarters in New York City on Sept. 24, 2025. (Ludovic Marin/AFP via Getty Images)
Despite the restrictions, Wold said UNGA gives Washington the opportunity it has "wanted for quite some time to have a large enough audience, and a sort of captive Iranian delegation" to make some of the essential points for why the administration pursued the actions it did against the Iranian regime.
Iranian state media also reported Sept. 19 that Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said New York held "absolutely no charm" for the Iranian delegation.
Baghaei, Mehr News Agency reported, went on to accuse the U.S. of using every tool to block the delegation’s participation, asserting that Iran’s attendance is a legal right rather than a favor.
Wold went on to criticize the U.N. for hosting state representatives hostile to American interests while raising security concerns.
"It's going to be one of those things that's fairly perplexing to most Americans," Wold said. "How is it that the representatives of what we have long identified as a hostile regime, but now one that we're actually engaged in combat operations against, one that has killed American service members, why is it that their diplomats get to come to the United Nations and exchange niceties with other kleptocrats or some of their other allies on the international scene?"
TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, left, shakes hands with the U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres during the General Assembly on Sept. 25, 2025, in New York City. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
Wold also added that the United Nations wants to "lecture us about international climate change or the need to trans children, but the other is happy to sort of serve as a forum for obvious violators of human rights and obvious regimes that are contrary to any number of internationally agreed-upon protocols."
Amid the hostility between Washington and Tehran, Wold said the gathering could also provide an opening for diplomacy. Trump is also slated to hold bilateral and sideline meetings with leaders from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to discuss regional security and the Strait of Hormuz .
"There's the hope that there'll be an opportunity for real discussion," Wold said of UNGA. "Everyone's hope, especially from State Department leadership, is that there'll be an opportunity to have a fulsome, sort of meaningful discussion with the Iranians, freed from some of the theatrics the Iranians have engaged in.

Wold expressed confidence in Washington’s posture heading into the summit.
"The president is best equipped for these moments. This is really where he sort of shines as a natural leader," he said. "He's not one to bend or to break. It's a precarious time for President Trump, but I have no doubt at all that he'll rise to the moment."

articles.title_zh: Boeing flags 737 MAX software glitch affecting landing navigation feature, WSJ reports
articles.content_orig:
Boeing said it flagged a software glitch last month on some 737 Max aircraft that could affect certain landing procedures, as the manufacturer seeks federal approval for the fourth and final model in its best-selling aircraft family.
The Federal Aviation Administration said Saturday that it is assessing the problem and "will take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern" and that it will review Boeing's proposed fix.
Boeing said the issue could arise after a missed approach when pilots alter a preprogrammed flight path, and that pilots must take additional steps to use automated tools on subsequent approaches.
"We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue," Boeing said. The Wall Street Journal reported the issue earlier.
The company said that pilots are trained to land without the automated system. "We are working directly with airlines to formalize a procedure that will allow pilots to reenable automated vertical navigation should this situation occur," Boeing said.
U.S. airlines told CNBC that they do not have Max 8 and Max 9 airplanes with the updated software tied to the glitch in their fleets. Airlines can revert some Maxes to the older software version.
All-Boeing 737 Max carrier Southwest Airlines said it is "aware of the issue and is engaged with Boeing and the FAA."
It added that "none of our fleet is equipped with Version U.14, including new deliveries of Max 8 airplanes." United Airlines also said it's not taking any Max aircraft deliveries with the new software.
However, questions remain about the two other models, the Max 7 and Max 10. The Federal Aviation Administration certified the Max 7 , the smallest of the Max family, in early August with the newest software installed. It wasn't immediately clear if the aircraft could be delivered or fly with an older version of software.
Additionally, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors earlier this month that he expected FAA certification of the Max 10 "very soon."
"We have been engaged with Boeing and the FAA and will continue to work closely with both as they evaluate this matter and determine next steps," Alaska Airlines , a Max 10 customer, said Saturday.
The issue comes after years of delays of Boeing's Max planes following safety and manufacturing crises, including the two deadly crashes of Max 8 aircraft in 2018 and 2019 that killed 346 people. A flawed flight control software system — which has since been updated — was implicated in both crashes.
There are 2,430 Max aircraft currently in service globally, according to Cirium.

articles.content_orig:
CNN had been scheduled to fly with Trump on Air Force One
Broadcaster CNN has been barred from travelling with US President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee on Saturday.
The move is the latest in a battle between the White House and the media after it was forced to lift its ban on some news outlets.
CNN was scheduled to fly with Trump for his trip to Tennessee for a college American football game until a note released on Friday night by the White House did not list the broadcaster on the media schedule.
The BBC has requested comment from the White House.
CNN has reported that no other outlet was listed as replacing them in the president's tentative schedule.
Last week, Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists from the White House after accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
All three media outlets said they were pursuing legal action and accused Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.
Four television networks that have a daily rotation of White House coverage alongside CNN - ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC - had paused their broadcasts of the president in solidarity with the banned outlets.
The White House then launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, ahead of the UN General Assembly in New York.
A federal judge has since ruled that Trump barring news outlets from the White House was likely unconstitutional and that the administration had to let them back in, at least for now.
However, the White House still denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals at a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday.
In a series of online posts on Saturday, Trump criticised the CNN and other media outlets dubbing them "fake news".
"FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE," he said.
A White House communications account earlier posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event and every press call".
Regular US television coverage resumed on Friday after White House officials allowed reporters entry.
The president is set to attend a football game between University of Tennessee vs University of Texas College at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville from midday local time on Saturday.

articles.content_orig:
Fox News chief religion correspondent Lauren Green reports live from Paris on Pope Leo XIV's visit to France, where he celebrated an open-air Catholic Mass before 800,000 people on the iconic Champs-Élysées on Saturday.
Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 people into the heart of Paris on Saturday for a massive open-air Mass, filling one of the French republic’s most storied public squares as he urged Catholics to openly share their faith in an "increasingly secularized society."
Flag-waving crowds packed the Champs-Élysées and Place de la Concorde as the American pope traveled roughly 1.2 miles through central Paris in the popemobile before celebrating Mass.
The Vatican estimated attendance at 800,000, roughly 200,000 more people than had registered in advance.
People of faith gathered in the streets, with families lifting babies and young children toward the popemobile as Leo made his way through the French capital.
POPE LEO XIV RECEIVES 'SYMBOLIC’ SPHERE IN CHARITY'S PUSH FOR AI TO 'PROTECT HUMAN DIGNITY'
Pope Leo XIV blesses a child and waves to the crowd from the popemobile as he rides down the Champs-Élysées Avenue on his way to the Place de la Concorde on Saturday in Paris. (Corbis via Getty Images)
"Seeing you gathered here," Leo told worshippers, he was looking upon the "heirs of France’s long and beautiful history of faith," according to Vatican News.
The pope called on French Catholics not to keep that rich inheritance to themselves.
FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH
Pope Leo XIV waves to the faithful as he arrives at Place de la Concorde to preside over Mass during his apostolic journey to France Saturday. (Getty Images)
"Let it overflow, so that those you meet may be refreshed and their thirst satisfied," Leo said. "From this beautiful city of Paris, I pray fervently that the living water of the Holy Spirit may flow throughout France."
The setting carried particular resonance in a country known for its strict tradition of secularism.
AMERICAN BISHOP ROBERT BARRON CALLS OUT ST. PAUL'S CATHEDRAL IN UK OVER NIGHTCLUB PARTNERSHIP
Pope Leo XIV presides over a Mass at Place de la Concorde on Saturday, during the second day of his apostolic journey to France. (Getty Images)
It is notable that the Place de la Concorde was an execution ground during the French Revolution, where devoutly Catholic King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette were guillotined. Today, the square is closely associated with the French republic and regularly hosts Bastille Day celebrations.
The decision to celebrate a papal Mass there drew criticism from supporters of France’s strict separation of church and state, who argued another site would have been more appropriate.
The images also offered a striking contrast with another massive Paris spectacle just two years earlier.
The 2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony drew worldwide controversy over a tableau featuring drag performers that Christian leaders and other critics said mocked Christianity.
POLL FINDS SHARP RISE IN YOUNG MEN CALLING RELIGION 'VERY IMPORTANT'
Pope Leo XIV waves to the crowd from the papamobile as he rides down the Champs-Élysées Avenue on his way to Place de la Concorde to celebrate a solemn outdoor Mass on Sept. 26, 2026, in Paris, France. The pontiff is making his first official visit to France from Sept. 25-28 with stops in Paris, Lourdes, and Metz. While in Paris, his agenda includes a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, a prayer service at Notre-Dame Cathedral, and the open-air Mass along the Champs-Élysées. The trip marks the first papal visit to the European country since Benedict XVI visited in 2008. (Corbis via Getty Images)
The French Bishops’ Conference said at the time that the ceremony "included scenes of mockery and derision of Christianity," adding that Christians around the world had been "hurt by the outrageousness and provocation of certain scenes."
The tableau was widely interpreted by critics as a parody of Leonardo da Vinci’s "The Last Supper," though Olympics organizers disputed that interpretation.
Leo’s visit comes as France experiences a notable increase in adult conversions even as the country continues a decades-long decline in overall Catholic participation.
Annual adult baptisms in France have tripled since 2016, reaching 13,000 this year, according to The Associated Press . Overall baptisms, however, have fallen sharply over the longer term, from 513,000 in 1980 to 186,000 in 2024.
YOUNG MEN ARE RETURNING TO CHURCH — AND IT COULD RESHAPE AMERICA’S FUTURE
A large crowd gathers on Avenue de la Grande Armee and watches Pope Leo XIV arrive on a giant screen with the Arc de Triomphe in the background in Paris, France, on Sept. 26, 2026. French and Vatican flags wave during the gathering organized for the papal visit to Paris. (Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images)
Leo thanked French families, young people, catechumens and new Christians for bearing witness to their faith in what he described as an "increasingly secularized society," according to Vatican News.
The scale of the pope’s reception was already apparent the night before the Mass as some 80,000 young people packed France’s national stadium Friday for a vigil featuring fireworks and a theatrical retelling of the country’s Catholic history.
"Thank you for your courage! Thank you for your presence," Leo told them in French. "Thank you for your faith. You are the saints of France!"
Worshippers gather on the Champs-Élysées in Paris as Pope Leo XIV celebrates an outdoor mass at Place de la Concorde on Sept. 26, 2026. Pope Leo XIV is making his first official visit to France from Sept. 25-28 with stops in Paris, Lourdes, and Metz. (Corbis via Getty Images)
At Saturday’s Mass, Leo invoked France’s Catholic heritage and drew on the biblical image of "living water," telling worshippers that Jesus Christ could satisfy humanity’s desire for "life, truth, unity, peace, communion, and happiness."
He also invoked French Catholic saints including Irenaeus, Martin and Francis de Sales while praising those who continue to work for "life, the family, truth, peace, fraternity and justice."
The sea of people rivaled some of the largest public celebrations to fill the Champs-Élysées in recent decades, including France’s World Cup victories in 1998 and 2018, according to the AP.
Worshippers gather on the Champs-Élysées in Paris for an outdoor mass celebrated by Pope Leo XIV on Sept. 26, 2026. The pontiff said it was possible to "live together in dignity and peace" during the service, which drew hundreds of thousands of believers. The mass is part of Pope Leo XIV's first official visit to France from Sept. 25-28, with stops in Paris, Lourdes, and Metz. While in Paris, the pontiff's agenda includes a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, a prayer service at Notre-Dame Cathedral, and other engagements. The trip marks the first papal visit to the European country since Benedict XVI visited in 2008. (Corbis via Getty Images)
Leo’s four-day trip to France began Friday with a visit to the restored Notre Dame Cathedral , the first by a pope since the devastating 2019 fire .

articles.title_orig: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Russell holds off Verstappen in super-close finish, Norris crashes out - The Athletic
articles.title_zh: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Russell holds off Verstappen in super-close finish, Norris crashes out - The Athletic
articles.content_orig:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli ’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.
Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.
Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.
The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.
A drag race to the finish line! 🍿 #F1 #AzerbaijanGP pic.twitter.com/Nb6xfkkpIb
Whether or not this performance is too little from Russell, it is almost certainly too late . The margin to the championship leader is now down to 66 points with a probable seven rounds – including one sprint race – remaining. It improves Russell’s chances of a championship from “unthinkable” to “remote”.
Russell has already written off his own hopes of beating Antonelli to the championship. He did not seem to have changed his mind or his approach after stepping out of his car victoriously.
“Win every race. That’s the game plan,” Russell said. “My team-mate’s had an incredible season, he’s been pretty flawless throughout, but now we’re getting to crunch time.
“I’m just going to focus on myself. If I continue giving performances like I did this weekend, at the end of the season I’ll be happy because it’s been a tough period for me and I’ll feel like I’ve come through the other side.”
In fairness to Russell, his eighth grand prix victory did not come entirely out of nowhere as he has been much closer to Antonelli since the summer break. With a bit more luck in Zandvoort and Monza, he may have been closer still.
“I think it’s just having more experience with this new driving style I’ve adopted and every race since the break I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength. I feel more like myself again,” he added.
Russell would have had an easier route to victory were it not for the two safety car periods in the second half of the race. The first came out after Alexander Albon slammed his Williams into the barriers at turn five on lap 31 of 51. That bunched the pack up and wiped out the 10-second lead that Russell had built up over Oscar Piastri’s McLaren.
As is so often the case in F1, and especially on street circuits, one safety car often brings about another. And so it was as Franco Colapinto’s enormously optimistic divebomb up the inside of turn one on the lap-36 restart took out not only his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, but also McLaren’s Lando Norris.
Absolute chaos at the restart 😵 #F1 #AzerbaijanGP pic.twitter.com/o4Q5MdHLnc
Norris had stern words for Colapinto, who has been handed a five-place grid drop for the next race in Malaysia, after his elimination. “There’s just some drivers that shouldn’t be in Formula One, to be honest,” the reigning world champion said.
“I think the FIA should start handing out bans for this kind of stuff. It’s careless, it costs a lot of money. All my parts are in the bin,” he added.
The greatest pressure Russell faced came after the second restart, after Verstappen moved swiftly into second. The Dutchman, who has yet to win in 2026, is not a driver anybody wants to see fill their mirrors at the best of times, let alone when trying to end a 12-week, six-race win drought.
Yet Verstappen could not find a way past. The most threatening moment of the final 12 laps was on the final push to the chequered flag. Valtteri Bottas put his Cadillac in the wall, bringing out double-waved yellow flags at turn 15. Russell lost his electrical boost on the run to the line but managed to hold off Verstappen by just 0.196sec, the closest winning margin for more than two decades.
As for Antonelli? He surely just needs to keep his car out of the wall, whatever Russell does.
It’s the Bahrain Grand Prix... in Malaysia. Here are the session times for that.

Saturday, October 3 FP3 – 5.30am Qualifying – 9am
Sunday, October 4 Race – 8am
A decent weekend for Haas, Red Bull and Lindblad. Williams should be happy with a point.
Too much for Russell to do but this performance should do wonders for his confidence. In fairness, he has driven well since the summer break.
“Win every race. My team-mate has had an incredible season, he’s been pretty flawless and now we’re getting to crunch time. I am going to focus on myself. It’s been a real tough period for me and I feel like I have come through the other side.”
“I am happy, it’s been very long six weeks. It’s been six weeks since I injured myself... this weekend I really too it step-by-step. It’s a track you can end up in the wall really quickly. It was a very slow build-up but it brought me here. I am very delighted.”
“We had a good race. The first stint was probably a bit difficult with the medium tyre but we worked out way into P3 and then we had a good restart... the yellow flag George lost a bit of boost in one corner. To the line I got close, but it was not enough.”
“It was amazing to be back on the top step of the podium. I want to say a big thank-you to my team. The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing. All, in all incredible weekend. It’s just having more experience with this new driving style I’ve adopted. Every race since the break I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength. I feel more like myself again.”

File photo of South African Police Service officers in Johannesburg
Police in South Africa say that they have found a woman's body in a Johannesburg suburb, the tenth in recent months.
The body was found on Saturday morning and identified by the friend with whom she had been at a bar the previous evening.
The local police commissioner said his force could not rule out the possibility that there was a serial killer on the loose, noting similarities across the 10 deaths in Ekurhuleni, as well as another in Soweto.
The deaths have sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in the country, which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world.
The latest body was discovered at a cemetery in the Tembisa neighbourhood north-east of central Johannesburg.
Police issued a statement a short while later saying crime scene investigators were at the scene gathering evidence. Officials have yet to publicly identify the victim.
The woman's friend told national broadcaster SABC that she recognised her friend's clothes from the previous night when shown a picture of the body.
"I don't know what I'm going to say to her children," she said while wiping away tears. "It's painful."
Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said that, at this early stage in the investigation, it was too soon to say whether the woman's death was linked to the others.
He told reporters that the other bodies shared a "similar victimology" that indicated a shared "modus operandi" of killing, which would allow police to determine whether this latest death was linked to the others.
"For now, it's not something which we can overrule to say there's a serial killer, but we cannot conclusively indicate as such," Lt Gen Mthombeni said.
South Africa has one of the highest homicide rates - with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.
But it is the nature of the recent killings around Johannesburg that has left many women there reeling from the growing death toll.
The 10 other bodies have been found in similar circumstances to one another since July. Most of them were found in Kempton Park, one neighbourhood over from Tembisa.
Many of the bodies were those of young women and almost all had suffered extreme violence prior to their deaths.
The deaths have placed pressure on the national government less than a year after ministers declared gender-based violence a national disaster.
While South African police statistics do not differentiate victims by gender, the South African Human Rights Commission said last week that 569 women were killed and 1,052 others survived attempted murder between April and June this year.
Three men appeared in court earlier this week accused of being involved in one of the nine murders, with police working to track down others who may have been involved.

In the latest roadblock, the White House announced in a Friday night note detailing the president’s schedule that CNN will not be allowed on Air Force One when Trump flies to Knoxville on Saturday for a college football game, the network reported .
CNN is part of a rotating press pool that covers White House events for major TV networks. No other outlet was listed to replace CNN in the memo, according to the network. Without a designated pooler, major networks won’t be able to televise his trip.
The network’s journalists were also stopped by a press wrangler when they tried to cover Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House for a state dinner Thursday night, the network reported .
The White House reportedly told CNN shortly before the event that it could cover the greeting ceremony but only with a photojournalist and audio technician, despite other networks being allowed to bring reporters and producers.
MS NOW also reported being blocked from the greeting ceremony. “The big question is — is this going to continue? Are we not going to be credentialed into these daily events?” MS NOW White House reporter Laura Barrón-López asked network host Symone Sanders Townsend Thursday night.
But CNN was allowed to cover Trump and Xi’s visit to the National Archives in Washington, D.C., on Friday.
The Independent has reached out to the White House and CNN for comment about the network’s coverage of Trump’s Knoxville trip.
Coverage of the White House has been spotty ever since Trump banned the three networks last Friday, calling them “fake news.”
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” the president wrote on Truth Social.
The outlets then sued to regain access to the White House, arguing the ban violated their First Amendment rights.
In an early morning ruling Thursday, U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly ordered the Trump administration to temporarily reinstate the outlets’ press badges.
But reporters were still denied entry later Thursday morning. By Thursday afternoon, reporters regained access to the White House.
The White House TV press pool had abstained from filming in solidarity with the outlets Trump banned until their access was reinstated. CBS served as the designated pooler Friday, filming Xi and Trump at the White House during the final day of his state visit .
Trump’s disdain for the mainstream press is well-documented, including his outbursts at female journalists for asking questions about the Epstein files and the Iran war. He has repeatedly targeted CNN’s Chief White House Correspondent Kaitlan Collins for “not smiling.”
But his attempt to ban several major outlets from the White House is unprecedented.
Former President Bill Clinton — who had an affair with a young staffer, Monica Lewinsky , in the 1990s that dominated the news cycle — said at the Clinton Global Initiative summit earlier this week, “There were lots of times when I wanted to ban the White House press corps.
“And there's a reason we have a Constitution. Because none of us are immune from being pissed off."

By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR
Published: 10:00 EDT, 26 September 2026 | Updated: 11:00 EDT, 26 September 2026
Hurricane Nolo is expected to cause 'catastrophic flooding' as the life-threatening storm nears the Hawaiian islands and over one million Americans this weekend.
A state of emergency has already been issued in Hawaii and forecasters now believe the strengthening hurricane could bring historic levels of rainfall, particularly across the Big Island (also known as Hawaii Island).
AccuWeather forecasters warned that the week-long deluge could dump as much as 55 inches of rain on the Big Island - just under five feet of precipitation.
If that prediction is correct, Nolo would be the second wettest hurricane in Hawaii's history, falling just behind Hurricane Lane's 58 inches in 2018.
The National Hurricane Center (NHC) said in a statement: 'Life-threatening, catastrophic flooding and mudslides are possible, especially in areas of steep terrain across the eastern and southern portions of the Big Island and Maui.'
Local officials on the islands have also urged residents and tourists to be prepared to evacuate flood-prone areas as the hurricane makes its closest approach.
Although Nolo is not projected to make landfall, AccuWeather has projected that at least two to four inches of rain will fall across the entire island chain. The hurricane is currently about 140 miles from Hawaii.
Both Maui and the Big Island are also expected to be struck by dangerous and sustained wind gusts reaching between 60 and 80 mph through Monday.
Hurricane Nolo is expected to become a Category 4 hurricane this weekend with winds over 130 mph
Residents in Hawaii began preparing for potentially catastrophic flooding this week
Nolo erupted into a tropical storm on Wednesday less than 400 miles south of the Hawaiian islands and has been slowly gaining strength throughout the week.
AccuWeather and NHC have both warned that Nolo will likely reach major hurricane status by Saturday afternoon, growing into a Category 3 storm with sustained winds exceeding 111 mph.
Saturday is expected to be the peak of the threat for Hawaii, as the hurricane makes its closest approach to land.
The worst of the rain and possible hurricane-force winds are expected to hit the exposed slopes of the Big Island's eastern side. Forecasts have predicted that this side of the island will see at least two feet of rain.
Maui, a major tourist destination just 30 miles to the west of the Big Island, will also see increasing rain and possible tropical storm conditions on Saturday, as winds range between 40 and 60 mph.
Mayor Richard Bissen of Maui County said in a statement : 'During this above-normal hurricane season, recent storms remind us that we cannot afford to be complacent.'
'Our top priority is the safety of our community. Now is the time for all of us to review household emergency plans, check supplies and make sure you can receive important alerts and information.'
National Weather Service officials in Honolulu warned: 'Leave immediately if evacuation orders are given for your area.'
Hurricane Lala caused at least two deaths and billions of dollars in damage from flooding and mudslides in August
Forecasters have warned that more than three feet of rain could fall on Hawaii's Big Island
A prediction of 55 inches of rain by AccuWeather would make Hurricane Nolo the second wettest hurricane in Hawaii's history
Hawaii's Big Island is home to more than 200,000 people, and the island is still recovering from the devastating effects of Hurricanes Lala and Lowell this summer.
The storm destroyed over 100 homes, damaged hundreds more and killed at least five people across the state, with the heaviest damage occurring on the Big Island during Lala's approach on August 15.
Downpours, flooding and mudslides, similar to what is expected during Nolo, led to more than 100 homes on the Big Island being washed away during the August hurricane.
Hurricane Lowell struck the opposite end of the island chain in September, causing widespread power outages and property damage on the islands of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau.
Emergency shelters have been opened on the Big Island ahead of the hurricane's arrival.
Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda said in a statement: 'If your home flooded before, or is at risk, consider moving to safer shelter before the full force of the storm hits. Because the ground remains saturated, flooding may happen rapidly.'
By Sunday, Nolo is expected to start moving away from Hawaii, although the hurricane will likely continue strengthening, growing into a Category 4 storm with winds surpassing 130 mph.
Rain and flooding will likely continue before gradually easing heading into the new week.

articles.title_zh: Trump rejects Iran’s seven-day roadmap to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.content_orig:
US president is said to expect renewed strikes after midterms
US president Donald Trump has said he has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in return for the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
“They made a proposal but I reject it,” he told reporters at the White House.
The US president was earlier said to be privately sceptical Iran would meet his demands to dismantle its nuclear programme, according to unnamed US officials cited by the Wall Street Journal.
Trump has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms in the US, the newspaper reported.
Meanwhile, on Friday evening, he published a post on his Truth Social platform with a graphic showing a map with the strait of Hormuz renamed as the “Trump Strait”.
During a three-hour meeting at the UN general assembly in New York earlier this week, Iran had proposed reopening the strait, which would have relieved pressure on global energy markets, and restarting talks on its nuclear programme within seven days.
In return, as well as lifting its naval blockade, Iran wants the US to permit the release of some of Iran’s frozen assets, restore the waiver that lifted sanctions on Iran’s oil exports and observe a “ceasefire on all fronts”.
That would involve the US president convincing Israel to end its attacks on Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon, a tall order, and allowing the strait to reopen largely on Iran’s terms, with the new route predominantly going through Iranian waters.
Saudi Arabia is also said to be concerned that the route deal is bilateral between Iran and Oman, and not with the Gulf states as joint signatories.
Reports of the rejection came as Iranian state media reported on Saturday morning that the Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, was on his way back to Tehran from New York.
After a meeting with UN secretary general, António Guterres, Pezeshkian said: “Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table, but given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States.”
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said ⁠late on Saturday that ​Tehran had seen ⁠an initial reaction from ​Trump ‌to ‌its proposal ‌but had yet to receive a response through mediators.
Iran ‌was waiting for the mediators ​to convey the definitive US position ⁠and would ​make a ​decision ​based on ​it, he added.
Earlier, a US official had ⁠said discussions with Iran through mediators were “positive and constructive” and, on Friday, Araghchi, had detailed the proposal to reporters outside the UN security council.
He said the seven-day timeline to open the strait and resume talks could start as soon as the US accepts Iran’s proposal. The initial steps would take about four to five days to complete, the strait would be opened on the sixth day and talks on the nuclear programme would start on the seventh day, he said.
This would include a protocol to allow UN nuclear inspectors back in to look at Iran’s damaged sites and the stockpile of highly enriched uranium.
The US naval blockade is putting intense pressure on the Iranian economy, while the seven-month-old conflict in the region has disrupted oil flows through one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes and is increasing the cost of living around the globe.
Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show Face the Nation, said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear programme and other issues, but would not accept “bullying or coercion”.
“Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that “we’re not supposed to develop nuclear weapons”.
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed ‌to end the war, which began on 28 February with US and Israeli attacks.
Since then the conflict has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran’s conventional forces and damaging its already ailing economy.
Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests. Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq were blamed for a pipeline attack that temporarily took more Saudi oil off the market.
The violence in Yemen has prompted a new humanitarian crisis, the UN children’s agency said on Friday, reporting a rise in acute malnutrition among children.
Trump has previously said he was in no rush to reach a deal, even as high oil prices fuel inflation. On the Iranian side, there are questions as to whether the hardliners who dominate the security forces would accept compromises championed by moderates such as Pezeshkian.
Diplomatic efforts surrounding the UN general assembly underscored the global stakes in the conflict.
Marina Dunbar contributed. With Reuters and AP

Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.
The so-called nor'easter is bringing "dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.
States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, both of which faced a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.
Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off due to the weather.
Residents on kayaks in a Beach Haven West, New Jersey, neighbourhood
The nor'easter caused widespread power cuts. More than 100,000 households, nearly all in the northeast US, have lost electricity, according to tracker PowerOutage.
The Federal Aviation Administration recommended air passengers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 2,400 flights have been delayed and another 1,199 grounded, according to FlightAware.
Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal flooding. Streets and homes were inundated with floodwater in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan on Saturday.
"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.
Streets and homes were inundated with floodwater in coastal parts of New Jersey
Flights have been delayed or cancelled due to the storm
NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."
In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power lines.
"Don't travel if you don't have to," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."
In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved the last game in their series against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday afternoon in Florida.
Waves pounded the coast in Massachusetts
A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.
Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead.

articles.content_orig:
O livia Rodrigo is, quite literally, unraveling. The pop star just kicked off the tour for her third studio album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love , and there was so much to unpack. The album, which was released back in June, takes listeners through every stage of a relationship, from the initial butterflies of a crush to the rush of falling in love to the heartbreaking disillusion of a partnership. Here, she took her storytelling to the next level, bringing her words to life through her setlist, stage design, and, of course, costumes.
Split up into seasons, the set opened with a stage covered in thousands of (fake) blooming flowers, upon which a Dilara Fındıkoğlu babydoll-clad Rodrigo charmed the crowd with hits such as “Drop Dead,” “So American,” and “You + Me = <3.” From there, spring turned into summer, and the artist changed into a bedazzled tank and hot-pink shorts for passionate, fiery renditions of “My Way” and protest song “Serena Joy.”
Fall saw a purple leather minidress from R&M Leathers with a choker (and fan favorites “Stupid Song” and “Maggots for Brains”), and winter rounded things out with a white pleated dress and some of the singer’s most emotional ballads, from debut single “Driver’s License” to this album’s heart-aching “The Cure.”
During this final number, the arena started raining on Rodrigo, and the downpour appeared to wash away her dress, revealing a red latex layer underneath. Designed by Hussein Chalayan and coined the “unraveled dress” by stylist duo Chloe and Chenelle Delgadillo, the piece was crafted from a water-soluble fabric that disintegrated when wet for a dramatic pre-encore finale.
For the encore itself, Rodrigo was back in spring, finishing things off (for real this time) with a simple white tank and low-rise jeans. Still wet from the rain, she performed a hit from each of her albums: “Deja Vu” from Sour , “All American Bitch” from Guts , and “Expectations” from You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love . Until next time.

articles.content_orig:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli ’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.
Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.
Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.
The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.
A drag race to the finish line! 🍿 #F1 #AzerbaijanGP pic.twitter.com/Nb6xfkkpIb
Whether or not this performance is too little from Russell, it is almost certainly too late . The margin to the championship leader is now down to 66 points with a probable seven rounds – including one sprint race – remaining. It improves Russell’s chances of a championship from “unthinkable” to “remote”.
Russell has already written off his own hopes of beating Antonelli to the championship. He did not seem to have changed his mind or his approach after stepping out of his car victoriously.
“Win every race. That’s the game plan,” Russell said. “My team-mate’s had an incredible season, he’s been pretty flawless throughout, but now we’re getting to crunch time.
“I’m just going to focus on myself. If I continue giving performances like I did this weekend, at the end of the season I’ll be happy because it’s been a tough period for me and I’ll feel like I’ve come through the other side.”
In fairness to Russell, his eighth grand prix victory did not come entirely out of nowhere as he has been much closer to Antonelli since the summer break. With a bit more luck in Zandvoort and Monza, he may have been closer still.
“I think it’s just having more experience with this new driving style I’ve adopted and every race since the break I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength. I feel more like myself again,” he added.
Russell would have had an easier route to victory were it not for the two safety car periods in the second half of the race. The first came out after Alexander Albon slammed his Williams into the barriers at turn five on lap 31 of 51. That bunched the pack up and wiped out the 10-second lead that Russell had built up over Oscar Piastri’s McLaren.
As is so often the case in F1, and especially on street circuits, one safety car often brings about another. And so it was as Franco Colapinto’s enormously optimistic divebomb up the inside of turn one on the lap-36 restart took out not only his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, but also McLaren’s Lando Norris.
Absolute chaos at the restart 😵 #F1 #AzerbaijanGP pic.twitter.com/o4Q5MdHLnc
Norris had stern words for Colapinto, who has been handed a five-place grid drop for the next race in Malaysia, after his elimination. “There’s just some drivers that shouldn’t be in Formula One, to be honest,” the reigning world champion said.
“I think the FIA should start handing out bans for this kind of stuff. It’s careless, it costs a lot of money. All my parts are in the bin,” he added.
The greatest pressure Russell faced came after the second restart, after Verstappen moved swiftly into second. The Dutchman, who has yet to win in 2026, is not a driver anybody wants to see fill their mirrors at the best of times, let alone when trying to end a 12-week, six-race win drought.
Yet Verstappen could not find a way past. The most threatening moment of the final 12 laps was on the final push to the chequered flag. Valtteri Bottas put his Cadillac in the wall, bringing out double-waved yellow flags at turn 15. Russell lost his electrical boost on the run to the line but managed to hold off Verstappen by just 0.196sec, the closest winning margin for more than two decades.
As for Antonelli? He surely just needs to keep his car out of the wall, whatever Russell does.
It’s the Bahrain Grand Prix... in Malaysia. Here are the session times for that.

Saturday, October 3 FP3 – 5.30am Qualifying – 9am
Sunday, October 4 Race – 8am
A decent weekend for Haas, Red Bull and Lindblad. Williams should be happy with a point.
Too much for Russell to do but this performance should do wonders for his confidence. In fairness, he has driven well since the summer break.
“Win every race. My team-mate has had an incredible season, he’s been pretty flawless and now we’re getting to crunch time. I am going to focus on myself. It’s been a real tough period for me and I feel like I have come through the other side.”
“I am happy, it’s been very long six weeks. It’s been six weeks since I injured myself... this weekend I really too it step-by-step. It’s a track you can end up in the wall really quickly. It was a very slow build-up but it brought me here. I am very delighted.”
“We had a good race. The first stint was probably a bit difficult with the medium tyre but we worked out way into P3 and then we had a good restart... the yellow flag George lost a bit of boost in one corner. To the line I got close, but it was not enough.”
“It was amazing to be back on the top step of the podium. I want to say a big thank-you to my team. The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing. All, in all incredible weekend. It’s just having more experience with this new driving style I’ve adopted. Every race since the break I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength. I feel more like myself again.”

articles.title_orig: Third person arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, as police say hanging was staged
articles.title_zh: Third person arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, as police say hanging was staged
articles.content_orig:
Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother of four, was found hanging from a tree in August
Warning: This story contains distressing details
The mother of a woman found hanging in a tree in Mississippi has spoken of her shock after authorities said they believed her daughter was dead before her body was placed at the allegedly "staged" crime scene.
Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother of four, was found hanging from a tree at an abandoned home in Jackson in August.
The discovery sparked widespread fears in the majority-black city because of the state's deep history of racial violence and lynchings. But on Friday, police said that Fortune had been dead before her body was hanged from the tree.
"I have more questions now than what I did before," her mother Christy Spivey told the BBC.
The Jackson Police Department said that the medical examiner who conducted Fortune's post-mortem examination had determined that her death was a homicide and that "the scene and the hanging were staged ".
Officials have not disclosed the exact cause of death or shared any potential motive behind the allegedly staged hanging.
Three people have been arrested in the case, all of whom are black.
"I was hoping to be more relieved," Spivey said, adding that the police had not specified how the three suspects were connected to her daughter - or why her death was allegedly staged in this way.
"Still no cause of death, no date of death - nothing," she said. "What actually killed her?"
Fortune's death left the local community on edge and lawmakers demanding federal probes . But the latest developments have created more confusion.
Christy Spivey told the BBC she was upset at how the police had handled the investigation
Spivey told the BBC that getting the update from the coroner that her daughter did not die by hanging initially gave her peace - at least her daughter did not die in such a gruesome manner, she thought.
"When the police called me, I started crying and thanked them and felt a little more at peace than I had before," she said. "I just hope they've got the right person/people."
When the latest details surrounding her death emerged this week, she said she was "starting to break down".
Police told a court on Friday that Fortune's death was thought to be as a result of a drug-related dispute. A detective said Fortune may have been killed over allegations she stole drugs.
Spivey rejected those allegations, but did acknowledge her daughter suffered from addiction.
"Tasia has an addiction - had - an addiction problem. She was trying to get better," Spivey said.
"If she still was doing drugs, which I'm sure she probably was, she still didn't deserve to be done like that. Nobody does."
She said her daughter was homeless at the time of her death, but typically bounced around other people's homes.
Her four sons, whose ages range from one to seven, are now living with a mix of family and friends. Two are in the process of being adopted.

articles.title_orig: 4 American tourists dead after building explosion and collapse in Athens
articles.title_zh: 4 American tourists dead after building explosion and collapse in Athens
articles.content_orig:
Four Americans were among the six people who died after an explosion and building collapse in Athens' tourist district of Plaka near the Acropolis on Friday, officials said.
A U.S. State Department spokesperson confirmed to CBS News on Saturday that their deaths were a result of a gas explosion.
"I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of four American citizens in yesterday's explosion in central Athens," Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to the Hellenic Republic, said on X.
"I extend my deepest appreciation to the Greek first responders who worked tirelessly at the scene. The U.S. Embassy is providing consular assistance and support to the victims' families."
The two other people killed were an elderly British man and his Greek wife who lived on the second floor of the three-story building, Greece's state broadcaster ERT reported.
The American family of four had been renting an apartment on the first floor and were preparing to go to the airport hours later Friday for their return to the United States when the blast occurred, according to the Kathimerini newspaper.
The explosion brought down the residential building and damaged properties and vehicles along the street. Two other women were injured from an adjacent building on Lysikratous Street, fire brigades said, according to the Associated Press.
The New York Times reported that the U.S. family was composed of a couple, their son and his girlfriend. Greek authorities did not immediately give their identities, ages or where in the U.S. they came from.
On Saturday, AFP reporters saw mechanical diggers moving debris at the site and thermal-imaging cameras deployed.
"We are talking about an incredible disaster," Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said.
Two nearby buildings were left in a dangerous state, he added, with inspections underway "to determine if they can remain standing or if they also have to be demolished."
The owner of the ground-floor apartment, Mathaios Artavanis, told the Kathimerini daily he was absent at the time of the blast. He said he had tried afterward to contact the U.K.-Greek couple who lived there, without success.
Video footage from the scene showed rubble strewn across the street, with parked cars smashed by falling debris. The people rescued by the fire department from the adjacent building were all tourists, resident Andreas Martzaklis said.
The pastor of a nearby church said this Sunday's service would be held outdoors because of damage to the church.
A year ago, locals in the Plaka neighborhood had warned the city and utility companies about the risk of gas leaks or short circuits, according to a letter by the residents' association published by Kathimerini.
The residents had urged a fire drill to identify possible weaknesses in the emergency response plans for the district.
A citizens' group said on social media that one resident in the street where the explosion happened had alerted authorities after smelling a possible gas leak.
The neighborhood is one of Athens' most popular tourist areas. The nearby Acropolis, one of Greece's best-known landmarks, welcomed 4.6 million visitors last year.

articles.content_orig:
By CAROLINE GRAHAM, US EDITOR THE MAIL ON SUNDAY
Published: 14:06 EDT, 26 September 2026 | Updated: 16:38 EDT, 26 September 2026
Sylvester Stallone has revealed he suffered from an eating disorder when he filmed his iconic Rocky movies.
The Hollywood superstar talked for the first time about the toll the tough guy films took in a candid interview in which he revealed he has struggled with his body ever since.
Speaking to the New York Times , the 80-year-old star said of his physique: 'It was my armour. I looked at Rocky: Very smooth, very normal-looking guy. And then I said, I think the character would start to become more vain.
'So I started to think: Design your body like a jaguar, a cat. Not big like Arnold (Schwarzenegger) but more feral and aggressive, and very limber and athletic.
'Then it got to the point where I became bulimic. You heard it here first. I got down to 2.6 per cent body fat when I was doing Rocky III, and I couldn't hold anything down.
'Or I didn't want to keep it down because I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness, literally an obsessive body-worship kind of thing.'
The actor admitted using steroids to bulk up his frame, adding: 'Nobody does it without additives and drugs, period.
'I don't care what they say. It isn't as though you're a junkie, but if you're going to work out and try to stay in shape for six months straight, and you're eating yoghurt and pudding, it's not happening.'
Sylvester Stallone has revealed he suffered from an eating disorder when he filmed his Rocky movies
The Hollywood superstar talked for the first time about the toll the tough guy films took on his body in a candid interview in which he revealed he has struggled with his body ever since
He said the impact on his body has been 'terrible' and that he 'takes a lot of pills to keep going'.
Stallone continued: 'But yeah, I've abused my body. I've had nine back operations, two shoulder operations, three neck fusions. Everything is held together with baling wire, but I still want to stay in good shape.'
Ironically, the muscle-bound star said he felt most comfortable when he appeared on screen as an out-of-shape police officer in 1997's Cop Land.
He told the Times: 'It wasn't until I did Cop Land, when I had to play the weakest guy in the room - partially deaf, overweight - that I felt somewhat liberated. Then things went sideways, and I just fell out of grace with Hollywood.'
The star, who also appeared in the Rambo films, has not appeared in a major film since Expendables 4 in 2023.
His new autobiography, The Steps: A Memoir, is scheduled for release on September 29. The title refers to the Philadelphia Museum of Art stairs he famously scaled in the original Rocky movie.
In the book, he talks about his troubled childhood and accused his parents of 'never nurturing' him to the point that he felt abandoned and neglected.
His father Frank was physically abusive and once punched him for bringing sandwich spread and not bread home from the store.
Stallone as Rocky Balboa in the third instalment of the sports film; he told the New York Times he dropped down to 2.6 per cent body fat while filming this movie
Another time, his father killed a cat. Stallone said: 'There was a cat making noise outside the house. He went out, got the cat, took it into the laundry room, shot it and left it in the wash tub. I think he did that to impress me. Like, you'll never be as tough as your old man.'
But he said that emotional trauma toughened him up and helped him survive in Hollywood.
He admitted he suffered anxiety and panic attacks which started at the age of 36: 'The first time was when I was 36, and I was watching dailies, and then all of a sudden I stood up, and the hair on my neck went up, and I started getting hot, and I go, I'm dying, this is it, I'm on my way out.
'And bang, down I went. Took a knee, crawled, rolled over, and now I'm in this dark movie theatre. Where the [expletive] did this come from? And then it happened again and again and again.'
He called his third wife Jennifer, the mother of his three daughters, 'the greatest woman ever'.
Stallone knows he is nearing the end of his life, telling the Times: 'All I can do is cherish every second because, let's face it, I can see the light at the end of the tunnel.'
